Make a report's content, from its spec file, without its code

Source: R/spec_code.R
tfl_content_run.Rd

Runs what tfl_content_code() writes: the same items, in the same order, each applied with do.call() – for a table, the data's steps (normalize_ard()), table_plan() and its layers. The two read one list of calls, so running the written code gives the same object; it is the quick way for a preview, the app or an assistant's check. A report whose content is its own code (content: !r) runs it, after the data's steps, and gives what it leaves in content.

Usage

tfl_content_run(output, data)

Arguments

output

A report (tfl_output()), resolved.

data

The data the content starts from: the ARD (or the normalized ARD when the content has no normalize_ard() item). With data.steps (R that makes data from the output's data.object, ard by default), the object the steps start from. For a figure, a named list of the objects its code reads: the datasets by their names in lower case (adtte), and ard.

Value

For a table, the rtfreporter::table_plan(); for a figure, the ggplot.

See also

tfl_content_code()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("cards", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ard <- cards::ard_stack(cards::ADSL, .by = ARM,
                          cards::ard_tabulate(variables = SEX))
  out <- tfl_output("T-1", "table", content = list(
    tfl_item("normalize_ard", list()),
    tfl_item("table_plan", list(cols = "ARM", rows = list(group = "variable"))),
    tfl_item("plan_cells", list(categorical = "{n} ({p:.1f%})"))))
  p <- tfl_content_run(out, ard)
  class(p)
}
#> [1] "table_plan"
